editorial:
Armed with only the word Tenet, you follow a secret agent through a world of spies, time tricks, and global danger. The story moves fast, jumping between countries and timelines, so you need to pay attention. John David Washington leads the mission with cool confidence, while Robert Pattinson adds charm and mystery. The action scenes feel big and loud, with fights and chases that twist time in wild ways. You may feel confused at first, but the movie trusts you to keep up. It is stylish, intense, and very different from a normal spy thriller.

The best parts are the huge set pieces, strong performances, and bold ideas. The downside is that the sound mix can make dialogue hard to hear, and the plot can feel too complicated. If you like smart action and do not mind rewatching scenes, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn the Protagonist has been running the whole mission from the future. He and Neil have already worked together before, but Neil remembers it while the Protagonist does not yet. They stop Sator from triggering the algorithm that would reverse time and destroy the world. Neil sacrifices himself to save the Protagonist, then reveals their friendship was always meant to happen. The Protagonist takes over Tenet, ready to protect the future.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves mind-bending action and big spy stories.
